scenarios.title: Who, when, what
scenarios.situation: A blog post claims Enochian is 'an ancient pre-human language discovered in a medieval manuscript.' A student asks for the documented record.
scenarios.prompt: What does the historical record actually show?
evidence: Between 1582 and 1589, the English scholar John Dee and the scryer Edward Kelley recorded extensive 'angelic conversations' — spirit-diary sessions in which Kelley reported communications. The result included an alphabet, vocabulary, and the 48 (or 49) 'Calls' or 'Keys' — the Enochian (they called it Angelical) corpus. It is an early-modern production, not an ancient manuscript find.
choices: Enochian was recorded in 1580s England by John Dee and Edward Kelley through scrying sessions documented in Dee's spirit diaries — an early-modern corpus (alphabet, vocabulary, Calls) with no ancient manuscript provenance; 'pre-human antiquity' is later lore, not record.
Enochian was discovered on clay tablets in Mesopotamia and dates to 3000 BCE.
Enochian was invented in the 1990s for a fantasy novel series.
John Dee worked alone in the 1200s; Kelley was his 19th-century biographer.
scenarios.why: The record is specific: named people, dated diaries, a defined corpus. 'Programming' enters as the lens — Enochian is a rule-governed symbol system, and studying it means studying its rules, tables, and transmission, not its claimed origin.
scenarios.hint: What is documented, and what is lore about the documentation?

scenarios.title: What makes it a system
scenarios.situation: A student asks why Enochian counts as a 'symbolic system' worth studying alongside programming languages, rather than just a curiosity.
choices: A symbolic system has a defined alphabet, combinatory rules, and interpretable structures: Enochian has a 21-letter script, recorded vocabulary with grammar-like patterns, and the Calls — long structured texts with internal repetition — making it analyzable with the same tools as any formal language (frequency, structure, consistency).
It counts because it is magical, and magic is a kind of programming.
It does not count; only languages with compilers are symbolic systems.
It counts because John Dee was a mathematician, so everything he touched is mathematics.
scenarios.why: The criterion is structural, not mystical: alphabet plus rules plus corpus equals a system you can analyze. That is the bridge from Enochian to programming — both are rule-governed symbol manipulation.
scenarios.hint: What three properties turn marks on paper into an analyzable system?

scenarios.title: Counting the angels' letters
scenarios.situation: You have a digitized Enochian Call transliterated into Latin characters. A teammate proposes frequency analysis — counting letter occurrences — to test whether the text has language-like structure.
scenarios.prompt: Is this a sound first step, and what would the results mean?
evidence: Classical cryptanalysis begins with frequency counts: natural languages show highly uneven letter distributions (in English, E far outruns Z). A flat, uniform distribution suggests random or constructed-without-language-patterns text; a skewed distribution is consistent with (not proof of) language-like generation.
choices: Yes — it is the correct first step: a skewed frequency profile is consistent with language-like structure (and lets you compare against English or Latin profiles), while a flat profile would suggest the text lacks natural-language statistical structure; either way it characterizes the corpus without claiming what the text means.
No — frequency analysis only works on ciphers, and Enochian is not a cipher.
Yes — and whatever the counts show will prove the text's supernatural origin.
No — the only valid analysis of Enochian is ritual pronunciation.
scenarios.why: Frequency analysis is descriptive, not revelatory: it measures statistical structure, which is evidence about the text's generation process, not its claimed source. Methodological modesty is the point.
scenarios.hint: What does a letter count prove, and what does it merely suggest?

scenarios.title: Dee's diaries versus the Golden Dawn
scenarios.situation: Two sources disagree on an Enochian table: Dee's 1580s spirit diaries show one arrangement; a Golden Dawn document from the 1890s shows a reorganized version with attributions added.
scenarios.prompt: How should a student handle the disagreement?
evidence: The Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (founded 1888) heavily adapted Dee and Kelley's material — reorganizing the tablets, adding tarot and elemental attributions, and building a magical curriculum. Their Enochian is a 19th-century reworking, three centuries downstream of the diaries.
choices: Treat them as two historical layers: the diaries are the 16th-century source, the Golden Dawn version is a 19th-century adaptation — cite which layer you are discussing, and never silently mix the reworking's attributions into claims about Dee's original.
The Golden Dawn version is the original; Dee copied it through time travel.
They are the same document; any differences are copyist errors to be ignored.
Discard both; only 20th-century versions count as real Enochian.
scenarios.why: Texts have biographies. The Golden Dawn's creative reworking is historically important in its own right — it powered a century of occult practice — but it is not Dee's Enochian, and conflating the layers corrupts both.
scenarios.hint: When two sources disagree, what question do you ask first?

scenarios.title: A grammar for the Calls
scenarios.situation: A computational-linguistics student wants to write a formal grammar covering the 48 Calls: terminals (the vocabulary), productions (phrase patterns), and a consistency check that flags any Call violating the patterns.
scenarios.prompt: What is the main methodological risk, and how is it managed?
choices: Overfitting a tiny corpus: with only 48 short texts, a grammar can 'fit' by memorizing rather than generalizing — manage it by stating the grammar's rules before testing, holding out some Calls as a test set, and reporting coverage honestly instead of tuning until everything passes.
There is no risk; any grammar that fits is automatically correct.
The risk is that formal grammars cannot represent any natural language.
The risk is supernatural: formalizing the Calls may have unintended effects.
scenarios.why: Small corpora punish the careless modeler: with 48 texts you can always write rules that fit perfectly and mean nothing. Pre-registration, holdout testing, and honest coverage reporting are what make the exercise science instead of numerology.
scenarios.hint: How do you stop your grammar from just memorizing 48 texts?

scenarios.title: Redundancy in the corpus
scenarios.situation: An information-theory student computes that Enochian Calls have lower per-character entropy than English prose and asks whether this shows the language is 'more efficient' or 'less expressive.'
evidence: Lower entropy means higher predictability/redundancy — the text is more constrained, more repetitive. Ritual and liturgical language is typically high-redundancy by design (repetition aids memorization and performance); redundancy says nothing about expressive power, which depends on the mapping between symbols and meanings.
choices: Lower entropy means higher redundancy — the Calls are more repetitive and predictable, as ritual language tends to be — which says nothing about efficiency or expressiveness; a highly redundant code can be perfectly expressive, and 'efficiency' depends on the channel and purpose, not on entropy alone.
Lower entropy proves Enochian is a superior, more efficient language than English.
Lower entropy proves the Calls are meaningless gibberish.
Entropy cannot be computed for non-modern languages.
scenarios.why: Entropy measures predictability, not quality. Ritual corpora are redundant on purpose — repetition is a feature of liturgy, not a bug of the language. The number describes the text's statistics; interpretation needs a theory of use.
scenarios.hint: What does predictability tell you about purpose?

scenarios.prompt: Using the systems anatomy method (whole → cut open → step through → pull apart), how would you systematically trace a failure in Enochian & Symbolic Systems?
choices: Walk the full journey: start from the trigger, verify each handoff in sequence, check dependencies at every step, and isolate where the flow breaks — then examine that specific layer
Restart all components — Enochian & Symbolic Systems issues are always fixed by restarting
Check the most common cause from memory and apply that fix immediately
Escalate to senior support — Enochian & Symbolic Systems is too complex to troubleshoot systematically
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Systems thinking means tracing the living flow: (1) Whole: what is Enochian & Symbolic Systems supposed to do end-to-end? (2) Cut open: what are the layers/stages? (3) Step through: verify each handoff — where does the expected output diverge from actual? (4) Pull apart: isolate the broken layer and examine it in detail. This method works for any Enochian & Symbolic Systems failure in Enochian Programming.

scenarios.title: Diagnose the Dead Working
scenarios.situation: A practitioner performs the Calls with excellent pronunciation, experiences vivid imagery, but reports that nothing in the working ever connects to the Tablet names she spent weeks constructing — the tablets feel like unused decoration.
scenarios.prompt: Using the four-layer flow (Calls -> Aethyrs -> Governors -> Tablets), where is the breakdown?
choices: The Call layer: pronunciation must be improved before the tablets can respond
The flow stopped between Governors and Tablets: the working invokes but never anchors — names from the tablets must be addressed and used within the rite, not left on paper
The Record layer is missing: she needs to journal more before the tablets activate
The Aethyr layer is overloaded: she should skip to a higher aethyr to get cleaner signal
scenarios.why: The working has energy at the invocation layer but no anchoring at the tablet layer — the diagnostic rule is to check the mechanical layer first. The tablet names and sigils must be actively addressed in the rite; paper maps only work when the key turns in the lock. Pronunciation is already strong, and changing aethyrs treats a connection problem as a signal problem.
scenarios.hint: Where does the flow stop — at invocation, at address, at anchoring, or at recording?
objectives: Diagnose failures at the layer where the flow stops
Distinguish signal problems from connection problems
evidence: Vivid visions, strong calls, tablets feel disconnected

scenarios.title: Close the Loop
scenarios.situation: A working group produces striking visions in every session but never pre-registers hypotheses, never compares visions against the corpus, and discards recordings after a week.
scenarios.prompt: Which feedback loop failure will degrade their practice fastest?
choices: The efficacy loop: they have no outcome audits, so they cannot learn which workings do anything
The coherence loop: without corpus comparison and preserved records, each session starts from zero and narrative drift is unchecked
The call layer: their pronunciation is probably degrading without feedback
The governor layer: they are not addressing governors by name often enough
scenarios.why: The coherence loop is the load-bearing one for visionary work: records plus corpus comparison are what turn experiences into a system. Without them, every session is a fresh start and the group cannot detect drift, contradiction, or genuine repetition — the exact failure the tradition's record-keeping discipline exists to prevent. Efficacy audits matter too, but coherence comes first in a vision practice.
scenarios.hint: What does the journal archive make possible that memory alone cannot?
objectives: Identify feedback loops in a visionary system
Protect the coherence loop with records
Order loops by dependency: coherence before efficacy
evidence: No hypotheses, no corpus checks, recordings discarded

scenarios.title: The Interpreter Problem
scenarios.situation: A scryer delivers a powerful vision. The group's senior member immediately announces its meaning, which conveniently confirms the group's current project direction — before anyone has transcribed the raw record.
scenarios.prompt: What is the systems-anatomy failure here, and what is the fix?
choices: A call-layer failure: the working should be repeated with the senior member absent
An interpreter-stage failure: the raw record must be fixed first and interpretation deferred to a separate sitting, so meaning cannot steer memory
A tablet-layer failure: the vision lacked tablet anchors, so meaning was invented
A governor-layer failure: no governor was consulted, so the meaning has no authority
scenarios.why: The interpreter is the most dangerous stage of the system: meaning assigned before the raw record is fixed contaminates the record itself — memory will reshape to fit the announced meaning. The fix is structural: transcribe first, interpret later, in a separate sitting, with the hypothesis logged beforehand. This is why the feedback-loop lesson puts interpretation discipline at the center.
scenarios.hint: Which is easier to corrupt: the raw transcript or the announced meaning?
objectives: Locate the interpreter as a failure point

scenarios.title: System Boundedness
scenarios.situation: A practitioner proposes extending the system: a 31st aethyr beyond ZAX, new governors for it, and extra letters to cover sounds missing from the Angelical alphabet.
scenarios.prompt: What does systems anatomy say about this proposal?
choices: Approve: the system grows through visionary extension, and more layers mean more power
Reject: the system's value is its bounded completeness — calls, aethyrs, governors, and tablets cross-reference each other, and additions that no other layer references are decorative, not systemic
Approve only the letters, since the alphabet is the weakest subsystem
Defer: only the group's senior member can authorize extensions
scenarios.why: The anatomy lesson's closure principle: every component's power comes from being cross-referenced by the others — a 31st aethyr that no call addresses and no governor administers is not part of the system, it is a separate invention wearing system vocabulary. Bounded completeness is a feature, not a limitation; it is what makes the system learnable and diagnosable.
scenarios.hint: What makes a component part of a system rather than a decoration?
objectives: Apply the closure principle to extensions
Distinguish systemic components from decorative ones
evidence: Does any other layer reference it?

scenarios.title: Resolve the Variant
scenarios.situation: Two manuscripts render the same letter differently — one with an extra stroke. Your tablet working depends on which is correct.
choices: Source hierarchy: consult Dee's original diaries first (primary), then contemporary copies, then later reconstructions — document the variant, note which sources support each form, and declare your working choice with reasons
Pick the prettier one
Average the two forms
Use whichever your teacher used without question
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Textual scholarship runs on source hierarchy: primary manuscripts outrank later copies, which outrank reconstructions. Documenting the variant and declaring your choice with reasons is the professional standard — silent adoption of any form is unscholarly.
scenarios.hint: Which source is closest to Dee's hand — and what do the others add?

scenarios.title: Declare the Standard
scenarios.situation: Your working group uses three different pronunciations of the same Call. Ritual coherence is suffering.
choices: Phonological standard document: start from diary glosses (primary), note Kelley hints, compare major systems, then the group declares one standard in writing with sources — practice follows scholarship
Loudest member decides
Use all three simultaneously
Abandon pronunciation — mumble
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Group practice needs a declared standard, and the standard needs a scholarly basis — diary glosses first, then documented comparison. 'Loudest decides' produces resentment; simultaneity produces incoherence. Write it down.
scenarios.hint: What would let a newcomer pronounce exactly as the group does?

scenarios.title: Audit the Numbers
scenarios.situation: A colleague claims a word's value 'proves' a theological point. The value uses an unattributed letter table.
scenarios.prompt: What is the correct scholarly response?
choices: Demand the table: gematria without a declared, sourced value system is uncheckable — reproduce the computation with a documented table, then assess whether the pattern survives independent checks
Accept it — numbers don't lie
Reject it — gematria is nonsense
Compute your own with a different table to win
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The issue isn't gematria per se but undeclared method — without the table, the claim is unreproducible. Scholarly gematria declares tables, shows work, and seeks independent corroboration. Neither credulity nor blanket dismissal is analytical.
scenarios.hint: What would you need to check the claim yourself?

scenarios.title: Fix the Corpus
scenarios.situation: Your digital corpus mixes three transliteration schemes. Search results are unreliable and analysis scripts break.
choices: Freeze, map, convert: freeze new entries, build explicit mapping tables between the three schemes, batch-convert the corpus to the single declared standard, then validate with round-trip checks
Keep all three — variety is fine
Delete the corpus and start over
Manually fix entries as encountered
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Corpus corruption needs systematic repair: mapping tables make the conversion deterministic, batch conversion fixes it at once, round-trip validation proves correctness. Manual piecemeal fixing never converges; starting over wastes the data.
scenarios.hint: How do you convert deterministically — and prove it worked?

scenarios.title: Study Deeply
scenarios.situation: You have one week before presenting on the letter 'Veh' — its form, sound, number, and correspondences.
choices: Five-step letter study: draw the form from diaries, record phonetic values with variants, note numeric attributions by system, map correspondences with layers labeled (Dee vs Golden Dawn), log pronunciation variants — one letter, full depth
Memorize one correspondence list
Wing it — it's one letter
Copy a website's summary
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Depth on one letter beats shallow coverage: the five-step method produces genuine command of form, sound, number, and layered correspondences. Presentation quality comes from primary-source grounding, not summary recycling.
scenarios.hint: What would make your presentation authoritative rather than derivative?
evidence: Diaries, Golden Dawn papers, modern scholarship

scenarios.title: The Ambiguous Letterform
scenarios.situation: While copying an Angelical word from a manuscript facsimile, you find a letterform that could be read as either of two letters — the manuscript hand is cramped and the distinction is genuinely unclear.
choices: Choose the reading that makes the better word: context decides

Check the word against other attestations of the same word in the corpus, consult a second manuscript witness if available, and if the ambiguity survives, log both readings with the uncertainty explicit — never silently resolve a doubtful letter
Guess quickly and move on: transcription speed matters more than precision
Omit the word from your lexicon: doubtful material is unusable
scenarios.why: Letterforms are data, and doubtful data is labeled, not silently resolved: the corpus check and second witness are the verification tools, and surviving ambiguity is logged as ambiguity. Choosing by 'better word' manufactures the lexicon; speed over precision corrupts the foundation the grammar lessons build on; omitting usable-with-caveats material wastes evidence.
scenarios.hint: What happens to every downstream analysis if the letter is resolved wrongly and silently?
evidence: Never silently resolve a doubtful letter

domains.name: The Angelic Calls: Structure and Delivery

scenarios.title: Parse the Call
scenarios.situation: You're given an unfamiliar Call passage and asked to identify its structural parts.
scenarios.prompt: What is the correct parsing procedure?
choices: Apply the four-part template: locate the opening invocation, identify the named powers/governors, extract the charge or instruction, find the license to depart — then note deviations from the template as analytically significant
Read it as poetry — structure doesn't matter
Translate word-by-word immediately
Skip to the 'important' names
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The template (invocation → naming → charge → license) is the analytical instrument — applying it reveals both conformity and meaningful deviation. Word-by-word translation without structural parsing misses the protocol logic.
scenarios.hint: What are the four parts — and what does deviation signify?

scenarios.title: Label the Uncertainty
scenarios.situation: You hypothesize a grammatical rule from six attestations. A colleague calls it 'the rule of Enochian verbs.'
scenarios.prompt: What is the correct scholarly stance?
choices: Inferred, not attested: six attestations support a hypothesis labeled 'inferred' — present it with the evidence count, test against new instances, and resist promotion to 'rule' without broader attestation
Agree — six examples prove the rule
Abandon it — six is too few for anything
Assert it confidently — confidence persuades
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Philological honesty requires epistemic labeling: six attestations = inference, not attestation. The hypothesis is valuable precisely when labeled — it guides testing. Promotion to 'rule' without evidence is how fields accumulate false certainty.
scenarios.hint: What does six attestations license you to claim?
evidence: Six attestations of a verb pattern

scenarios.title: Compare the Layers
scenarios.situation: A key term renders very differently in Dee's English vs the Golden Dawn version. Your working depends on the meaning.
choices: Triangulate: examine Dee's rendering in full diary context (primary), identify Golden Dawn's interpretive additions and their motives, consult modern critical readings — then declare your working choice with the comparison documented
Use the Golden Dawn version — it's the standard
Use Dee's — older is better
Pick whichever suits your working
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Layer comparison is historiography: each rendering reflects its era's needs. The scholarly move examines all three in context, identifies interpretive deltas, and declares a reasoned choice. Convenience-picking is the opposite of analysis.
scenarios.hint: What does each layer's difference reveal about its era?

scenarios.title: Work the 19th Call
scenarios.situation: You must explain how the 19th Call addresses thirty different Aethyrs.
choices: Recursive substitution: the 19th Call is a template with a variable — the Aethyr name slots in, generating thirty distinct workings from one structure; the system is parametric, not repetitive
It's repeated identically thirty times
There are thirty different 19th Calls
The number thirty is symbolic only
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The 19th Call's power is parametric design: one formal structure, thirty instantiations via name substitution. Understanding this reveals the system's computational elegance — it's a function applied to thirty arguments.
scenarios.hint: What varies between the thirty workings — and what stays constant?

scenarios.title: Standardize Delivery
scenarios.situation: Your group vibrates Calls together but sounds ragged — different pitches, timing, and pronunciations.
choices: Layered standardization: first the phonological standard (agreed sounds), then breath training (shared technique), then pitch reference (common tone), then rehearsed unison — each layer presupposes the last
Vibrate louder — power covers raggedness
Let everyone do their own thing — authenticity
Abandon group work
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Unison is engineered in layers: agreed phonology first (else different words), breath technique second (else unsustainable), pitch reference third, rehearsal fourth. Skipping layers produces the raggedness — each fix presupposes the prior one.
scenarios.hint: What must be agreed before unison is even possible?

scenarios.title: The Nineteenth Call in Practice
scenarios.situation: You are preparing to use the Call of the Aethyrs (the nineteenth call) for the first time, and notice its structure differs markedly from the eighteen world-calls you have memorized.
choices: Treat it as call number nineteen of the same series: memorize it the same way

Study it as its own instrument: it follows a different template (aethyr addressed by name, governors addressed, ascent opened) because it serves a different layer — learn its template, practice the name-insertion, and work it within aethyr workings, not as a generic invocation
Skip it until you have worked all eighteen world-calls extensively
Use only the opening lines: the full call is unnecessarily long
scenarios.why: The nineteenth call is a different instrument for a different layer — the aethyr-workings lessons establish it as the key for the aethyr layer, with its own template. Memorizing it 'the same way' as the world-calls ignores its distinct function; skipping it postpones the aethyr work unnecessarily; truncating it discards the template's closing movements.
scenarios.hint: Which layer of the system does this call address?
objectives: Learn the nineteenth call's distinct template
Match the instrument to its layer
evidence: Call of the Aethyrs: aethyr layer key

domains.name: Tablet Systems: The Great Table

scenarios.title: Extract by Geometry
scenarios.situation: You're asked to derive the Kerubic angel of the Air tablet's upper-left region.
choices: Apply the diagonal extraction rule to the specified Watchtower grid: trace the diagonal per the tradition's documented geometry, read the letters in order, and verify against published extractions — geometry first, names second
Meditate until the name comes
Pick a name that feels airy
Use a random letter generator
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Tablet names are geometric extractions, not inspirations — the diagonal rule applied to the grid yields the name deterministically. Verifiability is the point: anyone applying the same rule to the same grid gets the same name.
scenarios.hint: What generates the name — the grid or the practitioner?

scenarios.title: Order the Invocation
scenarios.situation: A working requires invoking a governor, a senior, and a kerubic angel. The protocol demands correct hierarchical order.
choices: Descend the hierarchy: Tablet of Union authority first (spirit presidents), then Aethyr governor, then Watchtower senior, then kerubic angel — rank order structures the working's protocol
Alphabetical order
Any order — hierarchy is symbolic
Reverse order — build up to the big one
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The tablet system encodes rank spatially and procedurally — invocation follows descending authority, mirroring the cosmology. Order isn't decoration; it's the protocol's logic made audible.
scenarios.hint: What does the grid's structure say about who outranks whom?

scenarios.title: Verify the Seal
scenarios.situation: Two practitioners construct sigils for the same name using the same tradition's rules. The seals differ.
choices: A construction error somewhere: deterministic rules on identical input must yield identical seals — the difference locates a rule-application mistake; find it by step-by-step comparison
Both are valid — sigils are personal
The tradition is incoherent
Spirits prefer variety
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Deterministic algorithms are self-checking: divergence proves error. Step-by-step comparison finds where the applications diverged. This verifiability is what separates systematic sigil construction from freeform art.
scenarios.hint: If the rules are deterministic, what does divergence prove?

scenarios.title: Log the Emendation
scenarios.situation: Your tablet source has an illegible cell. The working needs that position's letter.
choices: Emendation protocol: examine parallel tablets and geometric patterns for the likely reading, choose the minimal intervention, log the cell coordinates, original state, emended value, reasons, and principles — then version the tablet
Guess and don't mention it
Leave it blank — purity
Copy a different tablet's cell silently
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Illegible cells get principled emendation, not silent guessing or paralyzed purity: parallel evidence constrains the reading, minimal intervention preserves integrity, and the log makes the choice auditable. Scholarship is transparent about its repairs.
scenarios.hint: What makes an emendation scholarly rather than convenient?
evidence: Three tablets agree on the reading

scenarios.title: Use the Union Tablet
scenarios.situation: A working involves all four elemental tablets. The protocol references the Tablet of Union.
scenarios.prompt: What is the Union tablet's structural role?
choices: Governing layer: spirit names extracted from the Union tablet preside over the elemental Watchtowers — it binds the four into one system; workings addressing multiple elements invoke Union authority first
It's decorative — the four tablets suffice
It's a fifth element to invoke separately
It replaces the Watchtowers
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The Tablet of Union is the system's binding layer — its spirit presidents govern the elemental tablets hierarchically. Multi-element workings invoke Union authority to coordinate the four. Understanding this reveals the architecture: four subsystems, one governing interface.
scenarios.hint: What coordinates the four Watchtowers as one system?

scenarios.title: The Tablet of Union in Working
scenarios.situation: Your group works the four Watchtowers regularly but has never incorporated the Tablet of Union — the fifth tablet at the Great Table's center.
scenarios.prompt: What changes when the Union is properly included?
choices: Nothing: the Union is a theoretical construct with no working function

The working gains its binding center: the Union is the tablet that holds the four quarters in one rite — workings address the quarters through the center, and the rite's opening and closing run through the Union's names
The quarters become unnecessary: the Union replaces them
The working becomes four times longer with no added benefit
scenarios.why: The Tablet of Union is the Great Table's binding center — the angelic-hierarchy lessons place it at the middle of the four quarters, and its function is precisely to hold the quarters in a single working. Ignoring it leaves quarter-workings unbound; letting it replace the quarters inverts its role; the 'longer with no benefit' reading mistakes structure for padding.
scenarios.hint: What is a center FOR in a four-quarter system?
objectives: Incorporate the Tablet of Union as binding center
Run openings and closings through the Union
Hold the quarters in one rite
evidence: The binding center of quarter workings

domains.summary: Watchtower geometry, governors and angels, sigils, reconstruction debates — the spatial architecture.

domains.name: Scrying and Vision Work

scenarios.title: Run the Session
scenarios.situation: You're leading your first group scrying session. The skryer keeps interpreting mid-vision, and no one is scribing.
choices: Enforce role separation: skryer narrates only (no interpretation during gazing), assign a dedicated scribe for verbatim records, run timed intervals — clean protocol produces usable records; mixed roles produce mush
Let it flow naturally — structure kills vision
Interpret together in real time — it's more fun
Skip the scribe — you'll remember
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The protocol exists because memory rewrites and interpretation contaminates observation. Narrate-don't-interpret plus verbatim scribing is what makes records analyzable later. 'Natural flow' produces vivid mush — structured sessions produce data.
scenarios.hint: What will you wish you had in 30 days — vibes or verbatim records?

scenarios.title: Score the Vision
scenarios.situation: A vision included three checkable claims. Two verified, one failed. The practitioner wants to publish only the hits.
choices: Publish all three with the miss analyzed: selective reporting corrupts validation — the miss is data about the method's limits; honest negatives build the credibility that makes hits meaningful
Publish the hits — the miss was probably interference
Publish nothing — one miss invalidates everything
Reinterpret the miss as a hit
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The file-drawer problem is the credibility killer: publishing only hits manufactures a false success rate. Honest negatives calibrate the method — practitioners who report misses earn trust for their hits. Reinterpreting misses as hits is fraud.
scenarios.hint: What does the next practitioner learn from a hits-only report?

scenarios.title: Hold the Models
scenarios.situation: Two group members argue metaphysics: spirits vs psychology. Sessions are derailing.
choices: Model agnosticism as group policy: techniques are model-independent — agree to work the phenomena while holding different explanations; the practice quality is observable regardless of metaphysics
Vote on the correct metaphysics
Expel the minority view
Abandon practice until resolved
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Practice doesn't require metaphysical consensus — the techniques produce observable results under any model. Model warfare derails work; agnosticism preserves it. Groups that enshrine one model shrink; groups that bracket the question endure.
scenarios.hint: What does the session need — agreement on reality, or agreement on procedure?

scenarios.title: Save the Data
scenarios.situation: After a vivid session, the skryer 'remembers the gist' but no verbatim record exists.
choices: Compromised: memory rewrites vivid experiences within hours — gist-memory is reconstruction, not record; future analysis needs verbatim capture, so this session's data is lost to analysis (experience retained, evidence not)
Fine — the gist is what matters
Reconstruct it now in detail
Hypnotize the skryer to recover it
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Memory consolidation rewrites — vividness increases confabulation risk, not reliability. Without verbatim capture, the session yields experience but not evidence. The lesson is procedural: scribe next time, because this time's data is gone.
scenarios.hint: What does memory do to vivid experiences over 48 hours?

scenarios.title: Replicate It
scenarios.situation: One skryer reports striking results on a target. You want to know if it's signal or idiosyncrasy.
scenarios.prompt: What is the correct replication design?
choices: Independent blind replication: a second skryer, same target, no knowledge of the first's results, same protocol — convergence suggests signal; document both fully regardless of outcome
Ask the first skryer to do it again
Tell the second skryer the target and the first results
Accept the single result — it was striking
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Replication needs independence (no contamination) and blindness (no cueing) — same protocol, separate execution, full documentation either way. Repeating with the same skryer tests consistency, not validity; briefing the second skryer destroys independence.
scenarios.hint: What would convince a skeptic — and what would you need to run it?

domains.summary: Traditional scrying methods, record-keeping, and verification protocols for vision work.

domains.name: Ritual Protocol and Safeguards

scenarios.title: Plan the Working
scenarios.situation: A practitioner wants to 'do something Enochian' this weekend — no objective, no plan, no safeguards.
choices: Require the working plan first: one-sentence objective, selected components with reasons, timed sequence, contingencies, and safeguards — 'something Enochian' isn't a plan, and unplanned workings produce unusable results
Encourage spontaneity — the spirits guide
Suggest the most complex working available
Do it for them
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. The working plan template exists because vague intentions plus powerful techniques produce mess. Requiring objective, components, sequence, and safeguards before beginning is the professional standard — for teachers and self-directed practitioners alike.
scenarios.hint: What would make this weekend's work analyzable next month?

scenarios.title: Close the Loop
scenarios.situation: After intense workings, a practitioner reports restless sleep and intrusive imagery for a week.
scenarios.prompt: What is the likely cause and remedy?
choices: Unclosed sessions: skipped license-to-depart leaves psychological loops open — implement formal closure protocol immediately, add grounding routines, and enforce the 48-hour integration window; if symptoms persist, pause practice and seek support
Spiritual attack — escalate dramatically
Normal — ignore it
More workings will resolve it
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Closure is psychological hygiene: formal endings bound the session so the mind can file it as complete. Persistent intrusions after unclosed work are a known pattern with a known remedy — close properly, ground, integrate, and pause if needed. Dramatization helps nothing.
scenarios.hint: What bounds a psychological session so the mind files it complete?

scenarios.title: Structure the Group
scenarios.situation: A new working group has enthusiasm but no roles — everyone does everything, debriefs are skipped, one member is struggling silently.
choices: Define the four roles (leader, skryer, scribe, guardian) with the guardian explicitly tasked to watch group welfare, mandate post-session debriefs, and establish check-in norms — structure is what lets depth happen safely
Let it evolve organically
Remove the struggling member
Add more members for energy
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Role clarity prevents diffusion of responsibility; the guardian role exists precisely for the silently struggling member; mandatory debriefs catch what sessions stir up. 'Organic evolution' in ritual groups usually means the loudest dominate and the vulnerable suffer quietly.
scenarios.hint: Who is responsible for noticing the struggling member?

scenarios.title: Call the Pause
scenarios.situation: Your pre-defined pause criteria just triggered — but the working is going 'really well' and the group wants to continue.
choices: Honor the criteria: pause criteria are written calmly precisely for moments when enthusiasm overrides judgment — call the pause, close formally, debrief; criteria mean nothing if overridden when triggered
Continue — it's going well
Vote on whether to continue
Shorten but continue
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Pause criteria are pre-commitment devices — their entire function is binding when in-the-moment judgment is compromised. 'Going well' is exactly when criteria get tested. Overriding them teaches the group that safeguards are decorative.
scenarios.hint: What are pre-written criteria for if not this moment?

scenarios.title: Do the Integration
scenarios.situation: A practitioner does intense monthly workings but never journals, reviews, or integrates — each working starts from zero.
scenarios.prompt: What is the cost and fix?
choices: No compounding: without integration (journaling, 48-hour rule, quarterly pattern review), insights evaporate and the same ground gets re-trodden — implement the aftercare plan so workings accumulate into wisdom
More intense workings
Different system entirely
It's fine — experiences are enough
scenarios.why: The correct answer is A. Practice compounds through integration, not intensity — unintegrated workings are spiritual tourism: vivid but unaccumulating. The aftercare plan (journal, dream log, quarterly review) converts experiences into growing understanding. Intensity without integration is motion without progress.
scenarios.hint: What distinguishes tourism from training?

domains.summary: Designing complete workings: preparation, execution, closure, and the safeguards that make practice sustainable.

domains.name: The Thirty Aethyrs

scenarios.title: Choose the Entry Method
scenarios.situation: You are preparing your first formal aethyr working, to enter TEX — the thirtieth and lowest aethyr. Two methods are on the table: the standard invocation of the Call of the Aethyrs with the aethyr name, or an unstructured meditation on the name alone.
scenarios.prompt: Which approach does the tradition's method prescribe, and why?
choices: The Call of the Aethyrs with the name TEX inserted: the aethyrs are addressed through the Call, which is the system's key for that layer
Silent meditation on TEX: the Calls are for the tablets, not the aethyrs
Start with the highest aethyr instead: work downward from the top for safety
Use a crystal ball only: the Calls are unnecessary with proper tools
scenarios.why: The tradition addresses the aethyrs through the Call of the Aethyrs — the call IS the key for that layer, with the specific aethyr name inserted. Working TEX first follows the traditional sequence of ascending from the thirtieth upward. Meditation alone discards the system's own addressing mechanism; starting at the top inverts the graduated path the tradition lays out.
scenarios.hint: Which component of the system is the key for the aethyr layer?
evidence: The Call of the Aethyrs addresses each aethyr by name
TEX (30th) upward is the graduated path

scenarios.title: Addressing the Governors
scenarios.situation: Inside your working of an aethyr, you wish to make contact with one of its governing intelligences rather than drifting through unguided imagery.
choices: Wait passively: governors appear only when they choose, and any address is presumption
Call the governor by name, using the names proper to that aethyr — the tradition provides governor names and expects them to be used
Recite all 91 governor names in sequence to cover the field
Address the aethyr's seal instead: governors cannot be called directly
scenarios.why: The tradition supplies the names of the aethyrs' governors precisely so they can be addressed — named address is the mechanism, not presumption. Reciting all names is scattershot and breaks the discipline of working one region; waiting passively abandons the system's key-and-address design. The governors are the administrative layer between the aethyr field and the practitioner.
scenarios.hint: Why would the tradition preserve ninety-one specific names if they were not to be used?
objectives: Use governor names as addressable keys
Understand governors as the administrative layer
evidence: 91 governors of the 30 aethyrs are named

scenarios.title: The Blank Vision
scenarios.situation: During an aethyr working the scryer reports nothing — no imagery, no sensation, only a flat blank — for the full session. The group is tempted to call the working a failure.
scenarios.prompt: How should a disciplined practitioner treat a blank session?
choices: Discard it: a blank session contains no data and wastes journal space
Record it fully and treat it as data: blanks are a known phenomenon in the tradition, and the pattern of blanks across sessions is itself diagnostic
Repeat the working immediately with double the calls to force a result
Conclude the scryer is unsuitable and replace them
scenarios.why: Blank sessions are documented in the tradition and in modern practice — the record of WHEN blanks occur, in which aethyrs, and for whom, is diagnostic data (fatigue, wrong layer, preparation issues, or genuinely quiescent regions). Discarding them destroys the dataset that would reveal the pattern. Repeating immediately violates session discipline; replacing the scryer confuses a system event with a personnel failure.
scenarios.hint: What does a pattern of blanks across sessions tell you that one blank cannot?
objectives: Separate system events from personnel failures
evidence: Blank sessions are documented in visionary practice
Null results preserved in the journal

scenarios.title: Mapping Visionary Terrain
scenarios.situation: Your journal now holds ten sessions across five aethyrs, with recurring imagery: gates, rivers of light, and robed figures who give instructions in Angelical.
scenarios.prompt: What is the next methodologically sound step?
choices: Publish the visions immediately as new doctrine for the tradition
Build a cross-session map: index the recurring elements by aethyr, check them against the traditional descriptions of those aethyrs, and note convergences and divergences before drawing conclusions
Assume the robed figures are governors and begin obeying their instructions
Stop working those aethyrs: recurring imagery means the layer is exhausted
scenarios.why: The method is collation before conclusion: index recurring elements by aethyr, compare against the traditional corpus for those regions, and let convergences and divergences accumulate before theorizing. Publishing raw visions as doctrine skips the coherence loop; obeying unverified figures skips discernment; retiring a layer because it repeats confuses familiarity with exhaustion.
scenarios.hint: What did Dee do with repeated material across sessions?

scenarios.title: Ascending Order
scenarios.situation: A practitioner wants to work the aethyrs out of order, jumping to a middle aethyr because its traditional description sounds most interesting.
scenarios.prompt: What counsel does the tradition's method give?
choices: Follow the sequence from TEX upward: the aethyrs are graduated, and each prepares the capacity for the next
Order is irrelevant: all aethyrs are equally accessible to a prepared scryer
Jump freely but log the jumps: the journal will show whether order mattered
Work only the aethyrs whose governors you can name from memory
scenarios.why: The traditional working is an ascent: TEX (30th) upward through the sequence, each aethyr building the visionary capacity and vocabulary the next assumes. This is graduated exposure by design — the lower aethyrs are closer to the terrestrial, the higher more remote. Skipping is possible but abandons the scaffolding; the disciplined path earns the higher regions.
scenarios.hint: Why would a graduated system be arranged as an ascent at all?
objectives: Work the aethyrs in ascending sequence
Treat the aethyrs as graduated exposure
evidence: Each layer prepares capacity for the next

scenarios.title: Intensity in the Working
scenarios.situation: Mid-session in an aethyr working, the scryer reports overwhelming, distressing imagery and asks to stop. The session leader believes pushing through would yield the session's most valuable material.
choices: Stop the session immediately and move to grounding and aftercare: the scryer's stop-signal is absolute, and no material is worth a harmed practitioner
Encourage the scryer to continue for five more minutes to capture the peak material
Switch scryers mid-session and continue the working without pause
Record the distress as data and continue observing without intervention
scenarios.why: The stop-signal is absolute in every serious visionary tradition: the practitioner's welfare outranks the session's yield, without exception. Pushing through converts a controlled working into an incident, and the 'most valuable material' obtained under duress is the least trustworthy — distress corrupts the sensor. Aftercare and honest logging follow; the aethyr will still be there next week.
scenarios.hint: Who owns the stop decision in a session?
evidence: The scryer's stop-signal ends the session

scenarios.title: Interpretation Discipline
scenarios.situation: After a vivid aethyr session, two group members offer competing interpretations of the same imagery — one reads it as instruction about the group's future, the other as symbolic commentary on the scryer's personal life.
choices: Vote: the majority interpretation becomes the group's official reading
Neither — yet: log both hypotheses, check the imagery against the corpus, watch for corroboration in later sessions, and let the record accumulate before committing
Defer to the more experienced member: seniority is the tradition's tiebreaker
Treat both as true: visions are inherently multivalent and all readings are valid
scenarios.why: Premature interpretation is the interpreter-stage failure: the methodologically sound move is to log competing hypotheses as hypotheses, check against the corpus, and let later sessions corroborate or falsify. Voting confuses consensus with truth; seniority confuses rank with accuracy; 'all readings valid' abandons discernment entirely. The record is the arbiter, over time.
scenarios.hint: What did you learn about the interpreter stage from systems anatomy?
objectives: Let the record arbitrate over time
Reject seniority and voting as tiebreakers
evidence: Hypotheses logged, corpus checked, corroboration awaited

scenarios.title: Integrating the Working
scenarios.situation: Your aethyr series is complete: twelve sessions, full journal, mapped terrain, several corroborated details. The group asks what the work was FOR.
scenarios.prompt: What is the mark of a well-integrated aethyr working?
choices: A publishable manuscript describing the visions in literary form
A closed loop: the record yields refined questions, the questions inform the next working design, and the practitioner can articulate what changed in their capacity and understanding
A set of new rituals invented from the visionary material
The social prestige of having completed the series
scenarios.why: Integration means the feedback loop closes: record -> refined questions -> next design, plus an honest account of changed capacity. A literary manuscript without the loop is entertainment; invented rituals without corpus checking are decoration; prestige is not a result. The tradition's own standard is iterative research — Dee's journals show questions driving sessions driving questions.
scenarios.hint: What is the difference between a completed series and an integrated one?
objectives: Let questions drive the next design
evidence: Iterative research: questions drive sessions drive questions

domains.summary: Working the Aethyrs in vision: method and maps.

domains.name: Enochian Grammar and Syntax

scenarios.title: Word Order and Meaning
scenarios.situation: You are studying the translations of the Calls and notice the Angelical word order often differs from the English translation — verbs and qualifiers sit in unexpected positions.
scenarios.prompt: What is the sound grammatical conclusion?
choices: The translations are loose paraphrases and the word order carries no information
Angelical has its own syntax: study the word order across the Calls as data about the language's grammar, and let the translations illuminate rather than dictate the structure
The word order is random: the Calls were received in vision and never edited for grammar
English word order should be imposed when composing new Angelical phrases
scenarios.why: The Calls are the primary corpus of Angelical — their word order IS the grammatical data, and the translations are the gloss that helps decode it. Treating the translations as the structure and the Angelical as decoration inverts the evidence. Serious grammatical study works from the Angelical text outward, comparing parallel passages across the Calls.
scenarios.hint: Which text is the primary data: the Angelical or the English?
objectives: Treat Angelical word order as grammatical data
Work from the Angelical text outward
Use translations as gloss, not structure
evidence: The 19 Calls are the primary Angelical text

scenarios.title: Using Dee's Dictionary
scenarios.situation: You want to compose a short Angelical phrase for a working. You have access to a lexicon compiled from Dee's manuscripts.
scenarios.prompt: What is the disciplined way to use it?
choices: Combine any words freely: if the words are attested, the phrase is valid Angelical

Check each word's attested contexts, respect the word-order patterns observed in the Calls, keep the phrase short and anchored to known constructions, and log it as a modern composition — not as received text
Only use whole phrases from the Calls: no new composition is ever legitimate
Translate English idioms word-for-word: the dictionary makes this straightforward
scenarios.why: A lexicon is a tool, not a license: attested words in unattested combinations are modern compositions, and honesty requires labeling them as such. The discipline is to stay close to known constructions, keep compositions minimal, and never present a modern phrase as received Angelical. Word-for-word idiom translation ignores that idioms rarely survive translation.
scenarios.hint: What is the difference between an attested word and an attested phrase?
objectives: Distinguish attested words from attested phrases

scenarios.title: Translation Variance
scenarios.situation: Two reputable sources give different English renderings of the same Angelical line from a Call — one reads it as a command, the other as a description.
choices: Pick the reading that better suits your working's intent
Return to the Angelical text: analyze the morphology and parallel usages across the Calls, consult the manuscript context, and hold both readings as hypotheses until the grammar decides
Average the two readings into a compromise translation
Discard the line from your working: disputed text is unusable
scenarios.why: Translation variance is a grammatical question, not a preference question: the Angelical morphology, parallel passages, and manuscript context are the evidence that adjudicates. Choosing by convenience corrupts the working's address; averaging produces a reading nobody attested; discarding usable text over a solvable dispute is wasteful. Let the language decide.
scenarios.hint: What evidence could decide between a command reading and a description reading?

scenarios.title: Pronunciation and Efficacy
scenarios.situation: Your group argues about Angelical pronunciation: one faction uses reconstructed phonology from Dee's orthography, another uses a traditional pronunciation passed through 20th-century orders.
scenarios.prompt: What is the functional question to ask?
choices: Which pronunciation is historically 'correct' — authenticity is the only criterion
Which pronunciation does the group deliver consistently and confidently, since delivery quality and group coherence drive the working's psychological and ritual function
The argument is unresolvable: abandon vibratory delivery entirely
Use both simultaneously: alternate syllables between the two systems
scenarios.why: The tradition itself gives pronunciation through Dee's orthography and later working pronunciations — but the functional variable in a working is confident, consistent delivery by the group. A group fractured by a pronunciation dispute performs worse than a group united on either system. Decide once, document the choice, deliver it fully.
scenarios.hint: What actually happens in the room when the group cannot agree on pronunciation?
objectives: Decide once and document the choice

scenarios.title: Numbers in Angelical
scenarios.situation: You notice Angelical words with numerical associations in the tradition's tables and want to use number-letter correspondences in analyzing a Call.
choices: Apply the correspondences freely: every number pattern you find is meaningful
Use only the correspondences attested in the tradition's own tables, verify them against the manuscript sources, and treat findings as hypotheses requiring corroboration — not as discoveries
Numerology is superstition: exclude it from serious study entirely
Invent a complete system: the tradition's tables are incomplete
scenarios.why: The tradition does preserve numerical associations — but the discipline is to use the attested system, verify against sources, and hold findings as hypotheses. Free association manufactures patterns (the human mind finds them everywhere); blanket dismissal ignores the tradition's own material; inventing a system to fill gaps is the boundedness failure. Attested, verified, hypothesized — in that order.
scenarios.hint: What is the difference between finding a pattern and manufacturing one?

scenarios.title: Composing with Call Language
scenarios.situation: You are designing a working that needs an opening address in Angelical. You consider lifting phrases directly from the Calls versus composing new phrases from the lexicon.
scenarios.prompt: Which is the stronger practice, and why?
choices: Compose new phrases: originality shows deeper mastery of the language

Lift attested phrases from the Calls: they are the tradition's own tested instruments, their grammar is known-good, and their use carries the weight of the corpus — compose only where no attested phrase serves
Mix freely: alternate Call phrases with new compositions for balance
Avoid Angelical entirely: use English to prevent errors
scenarios.why: Attested Call phrases are known-good instruments: their grammar is established, their traditional function is documented, and using them aligns the working with the corpus. New composition is legitimate but weaker — every novel phrase is an untested hypothesis about the grammar. The hierarchy is: attested first, minimal composition only where needed, and always labeled.
scenarios.hint: What makes an attested phrase a stronger instrument than a new one?

scenarios.title: Productive Ambiguity
scenarios.situation: A key Angelical term in your working has two defensible translations — one martial, one peaceful — and the working's tone depends on which you intend.
scenarios.prompt: How does a grammarian-practitioner handle this?
choices: Resolve it before the working: study the term's uses across the corpus, decide the reading the evidence supports, state your chosen reading in the working design, and note the alternative in the record
Leave it ambiguous deliberately: ambiguity gives the working more power
Choose the peaceful reading: Enochian work should avoid martial tones
Choose the martial reading: stronger readings produce stronger workings
scenarios.why: Ambiguity is resolved by evidence, not by preference or by aesthetic: the term's distribution across the corpus decides, the decision is stated in the design, and the road not taken is logged. Deliberate ambiguity is abdication — the working's address should be precise. Choosing by tone preference is the interpreter problem wearing grammatical dress.
scenarios.hint: What does the corpus say about this term — have you actually checked?
objectives: State chosen readings in the design

scenarios.title: Learning the Language
scenarios.situation: A student asks for the fastest path to working competence in Angelical: memorize the alphabet, learn 200 words, or master the Calls' grammar.
choices: Vocabulary first: 200 words lets you read anything

The Calls' grammar first: master the 19 Calls as texts — recite, parse, and understand their structure — because the Calls are both the corpus and the primary working instruments, with alphabet and vocabulary filled in around them
Alphabet only: everything else follows from the letters
Grammar is unnecessary: pronunciation and intent are all that matter
scenarios.why: The Calls are simultaneously the textbook and the toolkit: mastering them as texts teaches the grammar in its working context and delivers the primary instruments at the same time. Vocabulary without grammar cannot compose or parse; alphabet without texts is sterile; 'intent only' discards the language the tradition spent years receiving. Center the Calls, radiate outward.
scenarios.hint: What single body of text is both the grammar textbook and the working toolkit?
evidence: Calls first, alphabet and lexicon around them

domains.summary: The Angelical language: structure, vocabulary, usage.

scenarios.title: The Shewstone Choice
scenarios.situation: You are acquiring a scrying stone in the tradition of Dee and Kelley, who famously used a shewstone (a polished obsidian mirror-like stone).
scenarios.prompt: What matters most in the choice?
choices: Historical exactness: only a 16th-century-style obsidian shewstone is legitimate
The stone's suitability as a focus: a dark, reflective, undistracting surface the scryer can gaze into comfortably for the session's duration — the tradition's principle, not its shopping list
Price: the most expensive crystal available signals the most serious intent
Size: the largest stone produces the largest visions
scenarios.why: The shewstone's function is optical and attentional: a dark reflective surface that holds the gaze without distracting it. The tradition's principle is the focus quality, not antiquarian exactness — Kelley used what Dee provided, and the working value was in the sustained gaze. Price and size are irrelevant variables dressed as criteria.
scenarios.hint: What does the stone DO in the working?
objectives: Choose tools by function, not antiquarianism
Apply the tradition's principle, not its shopping list
evidence: Dee and Kelley's shewstone: polished dark stone
Attentional focus for the receptive state

scenarios.title: Selecting a Scryer
scenarios.situation: Your group needs a scryer for a series of workings. Two candidates: one reports vivid visions constantly and embellishes eagerly; the other reports carefully, notes uncertainty, and sometimes reports blanks.
choices: The vivid one: stronger visions mean stronger workings
The careful one: honest reporting of uncertainty and blanks is the foundation of usable records — embellishment corrupts the dataset
Neither: use a rotating scryer each session for variety
Both simultaneously: two scryers double the data
scenarios.why: The scryer is the system's sensor, and sensor fidelity outranks sensor enthusiasm: the careful reporter's blanks and uncertainties are honest data, while the embellisher's vividness is noise shaped for applause. This is the tradition's own lesson — Dee valued Kelley's reporting discipline. Rotating scryers destroys comparability; doubling sensors without protocol doubles confusion.
scenarios.hint: Which candidate gives you a dataset you can trust?
objectives: Select for reporting honesty over vividness
Treat the scryer as a sensor: fidelity first

scenarios.title: Induction Trouble
scenarios.situation: A new scryer cannot reach the receptive state: they report feeling self-conscious, analytical, and 'too awake' through three sessions.
scenarios.prompt: What is the methodologically sound response?
choices: Push harder: longer sessions will break through the resistance

Diagnose the induction: review preparation, environment, and technique — adjust lighting, gaze duration, breathing, and pre-session routine systematically, and consider that some practitioners need many sessions before the state stabilizes
Conclude they lack the gift and dismiss them
Have them scry with eyes open in daylight: the state is unnecessary
scenarios.why: Induction is a trainable skill with individual learning curves: the sound response is systematic adjustment of the induction variables (environment, gaze, breath, routine, session length) plus patience across sessions. Forcing longer sessions fatigues without teaching; dismissal after three sessions confuses a learning curve with incapacity; abandoning the state abandons the method.
scenarios.hint: What are the adjustable variables in an induction?

scenarios.title: Leading Questions
scenarios.situation: During a session, the director asks the scryer: 'Do you see the great golden gate that guards this aethyr?' The scryer promptly reports a great golden gate.
choices: A successful confirmation: the director's knowledge guided the scryer to the true vision
Contamination: a leading question manufactured the vision — the report is now evidence of the director's expectation, not of the aethyr, and the session's data from that point is compromised
A test the scryer passed: responsiveness to direction shows a good working relationship
Nothing: scryers expect guidance and it does not affect the visions
scenarios.why: This is the classic contamination event: the vision now tracks the question, not the territory. From that moment the session's data is evidence of expectation, and honest record-keeping marks it as compromised. The discipline is open-ended prompts only ('What do you see now?') — the director's knowledge must never enter the scryer's field during a session.
scenarios.hint: Whose expectation does the golden gate now reflect?
objectives: Never ask leading questions in session
evidence: Session data compromised from that point

scenarios.title: The Working Environment
scenarios.situation: You are setting up a permanent scrying space. Resources are limited: you can optimize for quiet, for darkness control, or for impressive traditional decor.
choices: Decor: an impressive space puts the scryer in the right frame of mind
Quiet first, then darkness control: the receptive state needs freedom from interruption and controllable light — decor is the lowest priority
Darkness only: total darkness is the historical ideal
None: environment does not affect visionary work
scenarios.why: The environment serves the induction: uninterrupted quiet protects the fragile receptive state, and controllable (not necessarily total) darkness serves the gaze. Decor impresses visitors, not scryers — and a space optimized for display often compromises the working variables. Spend on what the sensor needs.
scenarios.hint: What does the receptive state actually require from a room?
objectives: Serve the induction, not the audience
Spend on what the sensor needs

scenarios.title: Session Length and Fatigue
scenarios.situation: Your best sessions seem to happen in the second hour, so the group proposes extending all sessions to three hours to capture more of that peak.
choices: Extend: more time at peak means more material

Do not extend blindly: the 'second hour peak' may be an artifact of warm-up, and three-hour sessions risk fatigue-corrupted data in the third hour — test with timed, logged sessions and compare material quality by hour before changing protocol
Extend but add a second scryer for the third hour
Shorten instead: all sessions should be under thirty minutes
scenarios.why: The observation is worth testing, not worth assuming: log material quality by hour across sessions and let the data decide the optimal length. Uncritical extension trades a hypothesized gain for a certain cost — fatigue corrupts the sensor, and third-hour material of declining quality poisons the dataset. Method decides protocol; anecdote proposes it.
scenarios.hint: How would you test whether the second-hour peak is real?
objectives: Test protocol changes with logged data
evidence: Timed sessions; quality indexed by hour

scenarios.title: Modern Adaptations
scenarios.situation: A practitioner proposes replacing the crystal with a VR headset displaying generative abstract visuals, arguing the technology is a better induction aid.
choices: Reject: only traditional tools are legitimate

Evaluate functionally: does it serve sustained, undistracted receptive gaze, and does it introduce new confounds (the generative content shaping the visions)? Test it against the crystal on the criteria that matter — and log the confound honestly
Accept: newer technology is inherently superior for visionary work
Accept but only for group sessions: keep the crystal for solo work
scenarios.why: Tools are judged by function: the question is whether the headset sustains receptive gaze without introducing content that shapes the visions — and generative visuals are a massive confound, feeding the scryer imagery that will be reported as vision. The crystal's virtue is its neutrality. Tradition is not the argument; the confound analysis is.
scenarios.hint: What does the generative imagery do to the dataset?

scenarios.title: The Debrief
scenarios.situation: After a powerful session, the group is excited and wants to discuss meanings immediately while the energy is high.
choices: Discuss immediately: fresh impressions are the most valuable
Secure the raw record first — verbatim transcript fixed and dated — then debrief interpretations separately, so excitement cannot rewrite memory
Skip the debrief: interpretations are forbidden entirely
Let the scryer interpret alone: group discussion contaminates
scenarios.why: The raw record is perishable and memory is suggestible: excitement rewrites. The method secures Layer 1 (verbatim transcript) before any interpretation talk begins, then holds the debrief as a separate, labeled activity. This is the same interpreter-separation discipline from systems anatomy, applied at the session level. Debrief is valuable — after the record is safe.
scenarios.hint: What happens to the transcript if interpretation comes first?
objectives: Secure the raw record before debrief
Hold debrief after the record is safe

scenarios.title: The Four Kings
scenarios.situation: You are studying the Great Table's structure and encounter the four kings (or princes) associated with the Watchtowers — one per quarter.
scenarios.prompt: What is their structural role in the system?
choices: They are decorative titles: the real work is done by the governors
They are the archic layer of the Watchtower system: each king presides over a quarter's tablet, with seniors beneath them — the hierarchy runs king -> seniors -> angels of the tablets
They rule the aethyrs, not the tablets
Each king governs all four quarters in rotation
scenarios.why: The Watchtower hierarchy is layered: the kings (princes) preside over their respective quarters, the seniors serve beneath them, and the tablet angels populate the working level. This is the terrestrial-administrative hierarchy, distinct from the aethyric governors — two hierarchies for two layers of the system, which is why the tradition keeps them separate.
scenarios.hint: Which layer of the system do the Watchtowers organize: the aethyrs or the terrestrial quarters?
objectives: Place kings at the head of the Watchtower hierarchy
Distinguish tablet hierarchy from aethyric governors
evidence: King -> seniors -> tablet angels per quarter
The four terrestrial quarters, not the aethyrs

scenarios.title: Working with Seniors
scenarios.situation: You plan a working that addresses the seniors of a Watchtower. A colleague suggests addressing all the seniors of all four Watchtowers at once for maximum coverage.
choices: Address the seniors of the single Watchtower relevant to the working's aim: precision of address is the system's mechanism — broadcast invocation is the opposite of the tradition's discipline
Address all seniors: coverage is always better
Address seniors only through their king: direct address is presumption
Skip the seniors: work only with the tablet angels
scenarios.why: The system's power is precision of address: one quarter, its king, its seniors — the working's aim determines the address, and the address determines what responds. Broadcast invocation across all quarters is ritual spam: it abandons the very specificity the hierarchy exists to provide. Address the seniors of the relevant Watchtower, by name, for the stated aim.
scenarios.hint: What is the hierarchy FOR, if not precision of address?
objectives: Address precisely: one quarter per working
Let the aim determine the address
evidence: Precision of address is the mechanism

scenarios.title: Matching Governor to Aim
scenarios.situation: Your aethyr working aims to recover a lost doctrinal detail from the tradition's corpus — a question of knowledge, not of practical art or prophecy.
scenarios.prompt: How do you select which governor to address?
choices: Address the first governor of the aethyr: order in the table is the selection rule
Consult the tradition's associations: select a governor traditionally associated with doctrine and knowledge, address them within their aethyr's working, and state the aim explicitly
Address all governors of the aethyr and let the right one answer
The aim does not matter: any governor can answer any question
scenarios.why: The governor tables preserve traditional associations with kinds of instruction — doctrine, arts, prophecy — and the disciplined practitioner matches the aim to the office. This is the same precision-of-address principle as the Watchtowers, applied to the aethyric layer. Addressing at random or in bulk abandons the system's own indexing.
scenarios.hint: Why would the tradition preserve distinct offices for the governors?
objectives: Match the aim to the governor's office
Use the tradition's associations as an index
State the aim explicitly in address
evidence: Governors associated with kinds of instruction
Aim matched to office, addressed by name

scenarios.title: Verifying a Name
scenarios.situation: In session, a scryer delivers a 'new' angel name, claiming it as a previously unknown governor. The group is excited.
choices: Accept it: the system grows through visionary reception

Check it against the tradition's tables and the corpus: a genuine addition must survive collation — does the name fit Angelical morphology, does it conflict with established names, does it recur across sessions and scryers — and until verified it is logged as an unverified claim, not used in working
Use it immediately in the next working: testing is verification
Reject it: the corpus is closed and no new names are possible
scenarios.why: New names are claims, and claims are verified: morphological fit, corpus collation, cross-session recurrence — the same discipline as the coherence loop. Immediate use skips verification; blanket rejection ignores that the tradition itself grew through reception; but until the checks pass, the name is a hypothesis in the log, not an instrument in the rite.
scenarios.hint: What would make you trust a new name enough to use it?
objectives: Verify new names against the corpus

scenarios.title: Two Hierarchies
scenarios.situation: A student confuses the Watchtower seniors with the aethyric governors, treating them as one hierarchy.
choices: There is no distinction: seniors and governors are the same offices under different names

They belong to different layers: the seniors serve the Watchtower kings in the terrestrial tablet system, while the governors administer the thirty aethyrs — tablet hierarchy for the quarters, governor hierarchy for the airs
The governors outrank the seniors in a single chain of command
The seniors outrank the governors in a single chain of command
scenarios.why: The system has two administrative hierarchies because it has two territories: the Watchtowers organize the terrestrial quarters (kings, seniors, tablet angels), and the governors administer the aethyrs (the airs). Collapsing them into one chain destroys the system's layered anatomy — the very structure the systems-anatomy lessons map. Rank across layers is a category error.
scenarios.hint: Which territory does each hierarchy administer?
objectives: Separate tablet hierarchy from aethyric governors

scenarios.title: Sigils in Address
scenarios.situation: You are preparing to address a senior of a Watchtower. The tradition provides the senior's sigil as well as the name.
scenarios.prompt: How do the sigil and the name work together in the address?
choices: The sigil replaces the name: trace it silently and no vocal address is needed
Name and sigil are complementary instruments: the name is the vocal address, the sigil is the visual anchor — used together they focus both the voice and the gaze on the same target
The sigil is decoration: only the name has operative function
Use one or the other at random: they are interchangeable
scenarios.why: The tradition's instruments are multi-modal by design: the spoken name addresses, the traced or gazed-upon sigil focuses — voice and eye converging on one target. This is the map-and-key logic again: the sigil is a precise visual key, the name the vocal one. Treating them as interchangeable or redundant misses the system's deliberate redundancy.
scenarios.hint: What does each instrument engage: the voice or the eye?
objectives: Use name and sigil as complementary instruments
Focus voice and gaze on one target
evidence: Convergent focus on the addressed intelligence

scenarios.title: Posture Toward the Hierarchy
scenarios.situation: A practitioner oscillates between two postures: commanding the angels as subordinates, and worshipping them as divine.
scenarios.prompt: What posture does the tradition prescribe?
choices: Command: the practitioner is the operator and the hierarchy obeys
Worship: the hierarchy is divine and the practitioner submits
Formal respectful address: neither command nor worship — the practitioner petitions with the authority of the working's design and the tradition's forms, as Dee did
It does not matter: results are the same regardless of posture
scenarios.why: The journals show Dee's posture: formal, respectful, petitionary — using the tradition's own forms of address, neither commanding the intelligences nor worshipping them. Command corrupts the relationship into coercion (and the tradition warns against it); worship abdicates the practitioner's responsibility for the working. The middle posture is the tradition's own.
scenarios.hint: What posture do Dee's journals actually show?

scenarios.title: The Corrupted Name
scenarios.situation: While preparing a working you discover that the governor name in your working copy differs by one letter from the name in two independent manuscript sources.
choices: Use your copy: the difference of one letter cannot matter
Use the manuscript consensus: names are addresses, and a corrupted address misdirects the working — correct your copy, note the variant in the journal, and verify before the session
Use both versions to cover the possibilities
Abandon the working: corrupted sources mean the tradition is unreliable
scenarios.why: Names are addresses: a one-letter corruption is a wrong address, and the working's precision depends on exact names — this is why the governor protocol stresses sourced tables. The fix is mechanical: adopt the manuscript consensus, log the variant, verify. Using both is ritual hedging; abandoning the tradition over a copyist's error is disproportionate.
scenarios.hint: If names are addresses, what is a misspelled name?
