scenarios.title: Designing Daily Practice
scenarios.situation: You have thirty minutes a day for Enochian work alongside a full-time job. You are tempted to do a little of everything each day: some alphabet, a call, tablet study, and scrying.
choices: Rotate daily through everything: variety keeps the practice alive

Block the week by layer: e.g., two days of call recitation and pronunciation, two days of tablet/corpus study, one day of scrying practice, with rest days — depth per session beats breadth per session
Do only scrying daily: visions are the point of the system
Study only: practice can wait until you fully understand the system
scenarios.why: Thirty minutes rewards depth, not breadth: blocked days let each layer get real work — pronunciation grooves, tablet study accumulates, scrying sessions have proper induction time. Daily dabbling in everything keeps every layer shallow forever. And 'study only until understanding' postpones the practice that produces understanding.
scenarios.hint: What does thirty minutes actually allow: depth or breadth?
objectives: Choose depth per session over breadth

scenarios.title: The Journal Standard
scenarios.situation: Your Enochian journal is a mix of dated entries, undated fragments, interpretations mixed into transcripts, and loose sheets.
scenarios.prompt: What is the minimum viable journal discipline?
choices: It is fine: creative practitioners should not be constrained by bureaucracy
Every entry dated; transcripts verbatim and separate from interpretation; loose material filed by session; a monthly index — the journal is the system's memory and must be auditable
Rewrite it all neatly at year end: the final form is what matters
Keep only the successful sessions: failures clutter the record
scenarios.why: The journal is the system made durable: dated entries, separated layers, filed material, and an index are what make the record auditable — by you in six months, by a collaborator, by the coherence loop. Creative freedom belongs in the working, not in the archive. And failures are the most instructive entries; discarding them falsifies the dataset.
scenarios.hint: Who reads your journal in six months, and what will they need?
evidence: Undated fragments, mixed layers, loose sheets

scenarios.title: Approaching the Heptarchia
scenarios.situation: You have worked the Calls and tablets for a year and are considering the Heptarchia Mystica — the tradition's system of planetary kings, princes, and ministers with its own tablets and calls.
choices: Begin immediately: it is the most powerful part of the system and you are ready

Treat it as an advanced curriculum: consolidate the foundational layers first (calls fluent, tablets constructed and used, aethyr method established), study the Heptarchic material as a system before working it, and enter it as a new course of study — not as an upgrade
Skip it: the Heptarchia is a historical curiosity with no working value
Work it simultaneously with everything else: parallel tracks accelerate
scenarios.why: The Heptarchia Mystica is a complete subsystem — its own kings, ministers, tablets, and calls — and the sound approach treats it as advanced curriculum: foundations consolidated first, studied as a system, entered deliberately. Rushing in confuses novelty with readiness; skipping it discards part of the tradition; parallel-tracking everything keeps all tracks shallow.
scenarios.hint: What does 'advanced' mean in a graduated system?
objectives: Study it as a complete subsystem
Enter deliberately, not as an upgrade
evidence: Heptarchia Mystica: planetary kings, ministers, tablets
Calls fluent, tablets used, aethyr method set

scenarios.title: The Combined Working
scenarios.situation: You are designing a major working that combines a Watchtower tablet operation with an aethyr ascent in a single rite.
scenarios.prompt: What design principle governs the combination?
choices: Combine freely: more layers mean more power

Sequence and separate: give each subsystem its own phase with its own opening and closing, ordered by the system's anatomy (terrestrial/tablet work before aethyric ascent, or the reverse by design) — combined workings are sequenced workings, not blended ones
Blend them: open everything at once for maximum intensity
Do not combine: the subsystems must never meet in one rite
scenarios.why: Combined workings are sequenced workings: each subsystem gets its own phase, its own opening and closing, in an order justified by the system's anatomy. Blending everything at once destroys diagnosability — when something happens, no layer can be credited. Never combining is over-cautious; the tradition's major workings are precisely these sequenced integrations.
scenarios.hint: If something happens in a blended rite, which layer gets the credit?
objectives: Open and close each subsystem separately

scenarios.title: The Plateau
scenarios.situation: After eighteen months of steady practice, your visions have plateaued: sessions are consistent but unremarkable, and no new material has emerged for months.
choices: As failure: the system has stopped working for you

As data: audit the practice first (preparation quality, journal discipline, induction variables), then consider that plateaus are a documented phase — consolidation before the next ascent — and adjust one variable at a time
As a sign to escalate: attempt the highest aethyrs immediately
As a sign to quit scrying and switch to pure scholarship
scenarios.why: Plateaus are data before they are verdicts: the disciplined response audits the practice variables first (most plateaus are preparation or journal decay), recognizes consolidation as a real phase of graduated systems, and changes one variable at a time. Escalation as a response to flatness is the classic error — it treats the system like a stimulant.
scenarios.hint: What changed in your practice in the months before the plateau?
objectives: Change one variable at a time

scenarios.title: Starting a Working Group
scenarios.situation: Three practitioners want to form an Enochian working group. They ask you for the founding disciplines.
choices: Enthusiasm and commitment: the rest sorts itself out

Agreed protocol (openings, closings, stop-signals), separated roles (scryer, director, journal), the three-layer record standard, interpretation deferred to separate sittings, and a written code of practice — structure before spontaneity
A charismatic leader: groups need a single authority
Secrecy oaths: the work must be protected from outsiders
scenarios.why: Groups fail on structure, not on enthusiasm: the non-negotiables are protocol, separated roles, record standards, deferred interpretation, and a written code — the disciplines that keep three people's subjectivity from contaminating each other. Charisma is not a method; secrecy oaths protect egos, while record discipline protects the work.
scenarios.hint: What keeps three subjectivities from contaminating each other?
objectives: Found groups on protocol and roles
Write the code of practice first

scenarios.title: The Long Curriculum
scenarios.situation: A student asks for a three-year Enochian curriculum. They want to 'do it all' in year one.
scenarios.prompt: How do you structure the three years?
choices: Year 1: foundations (alphabet, calls as texts, pronunciation, journal discipline); Year 2: tablets constructed and worked, aethyr method established, governor protocol; Year 3: Heptarchia, combined workings, teaching and transmission — each year consolidates before the next begins
Year 1: everything at introductory level; Year 2: everything again deeper; Year 3: mastery
Let the student follow their interests each year: motivation is the curriculum
Three years is excessive: compress it all into one intensive year
scenarios.why: The graduated system gets a graduated curriculum: foundations, then the working layers, then the advanced integrations and transmission — each year consolidating the last. 'Everything at once, then deeper' keeps everything shallow twice. Interest-led study has a place, but the system's dependencies (calls before aethyrs, tablets before combined workings) are not optional.
scenarios.hint: What depends on what in this system?
objectives: Consolidate each year before the next

scenarios.title: Teaching the System
scenarios.situation: After three years of solid practice, you are asked to teach Enochian basics to newcomers.
scenarios.prompt: What is the responsible teaching stance?
choices: Teach everything you know: generosity is the tradition

Teach the foundations you have actually consolidated (alphabet, calls, journal method, basic protocol), be explicit about the boundaries of your competence, and teach the method of verification alongside the content — transmission includes the discernment disciplines
Teach only theory: practice transmission requires a lineage you lack
Decline: three years is insufficient to teach anything
scenarios.why: Responsible transmission teaches what is consolidated, names the boundaries honestly, and — crucially — transmits the verification method along with the content: students who learn the discernment disciplines can outgrow their teacher safely. Teaching everything indiscriminately transmits unconsolidated material; teaching only theory withholds the practice; false modesty that declines to teach anything wastes three years of real competence.
scenarios.hint: What must a student receive besides content?

lessons.title: Enochian & Symbolic Systems — Core concepts
concepts: The documented record: between 1582 and 1589, John Dee — mathematician, astronomer, advisor to Elizabeth I — and Edward Kelley recorded 'angelic conversations' in spirit diaries, producing the Enochian (they called it Angelical) corpus: a 21-letter script, vocabulary, and the 48/49 Calls or Keys. It is an early-modern production; claims of ancient provenance are later lore.

A symbolic system is defined structurally: a finite alphabet, combinatory rules, and a corpus exhibiting patterns. Enochian qualifies for analysis on these grounds — the same grounds that qualify a programming language — regardless of what one believes about its claimed origin.

Texts have biographies. The Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (from 1888) reorganized Dee and Kelley's tablets, added elemental and tarot attributions, and built a curriculum on the result. Golden Dawn Enochian is a 19th-century adaptation — historically significant, but a distinct layer from the 1580s diaries.

'Programming' here means rule-governed symbol manipulation: tables, keys, permutations, grammars. Studying Enochian computationally — frequency profiles, structural grammars, combinatorics of the tablets — is continuous with cryptanalysis and formal-language theory, not with belief.

Small corpora demand methodological discipline: with only dozens of short Calls, grammars and statistics overfit effortlessly. Pre-state rules, hold out test material, report coverage honestly — the same hygiene as any machine-learning evaluation.

Information theory gives neutral descriptors: entropy measures predictability, redundancy measures constraint. Ritual language is high-redundancy by design. These numbers characterize the corpus; they do not adjudicate its claimed source — method knows its limits.

example.code:
python3 - <<'EOF'
# Frequency profile of a transliterated Enochian-style sample
sample = "ol sonf vorsg goho iad balt lansh calz vonpho"
from collections import Counter
freq = Counter(c for c in sample if c.isalpha())
total = sum(freq.values())
for ch, n in freq.most_common(8):
    print(f"{ch}: {n/total:.2f}")
print("skewed = language-like structure; flat = suspicious")
EOF
example.walkthrough: Counting letter frequencies is cryptanalysis' first move: natural language is uneven (some letters dominate), random text is flat. The profile describes the corpus's statistical structure — evidence about process, not about provenance.

pitfalls: Common trap: treating Golden Dawn attributions as Dee's originals — three centuries of adaptation separate the layers; cite the layer you mean.

Common trap: letting analysis drift into endorsement — statistical structure in the corpus is a fact about the text; claims about angels are claims about the world, and the course asserts only the former.
Common trap: overfitting the tiny corpus — with 48 Calls, any sufficiently elaborate grammar 'fits'; unfalsifiable fitting is numerology, not linguistics.
Common trap: reading entropy as quality — low entropy means high redundancy (typical of ritual language), not superiority, inferiority, or meaninglessness.
